Advanced CRUD: paging, ownership and concurrency

Try paging, ownership checks and an edit with an out-of-date version.

Open interactive lesson and complete code

What you are building

A student API with accounts and protected records

Register an account and log in. Each signed-in user works with their own students. The API also shows paging and checks whether a record has changed before saving an edit.

Accounts and student rows are stored in SQLite. Keep the access token for later requests.

Check the result

Register, log in, copy the token into a request and create a student belonging to that account.

An advanced API is not just more endpoints. It must cope with large lists, simultaneous edits, cancelled requests and users who must not see each other’s records.

How to test this example in Visual Studio

Download the project below, extract it into its own folder, then open StudyLab.csproj. Wait for NuGet restore. Choose Build → Build Solution. For console projects choose Start Without Debugging. For API projects use View → Terminal, make sure the terminal is in the folder containing StudyLab.csproj, then run the command shown in the lesson. Do not paste all files into Program.cs: use the exact file names displayed below.

Install and create the right project

  • Install Visual Studio with ASP.NET and web development and a .NET 10-compatible SDK. For WPF also install .NET desktop development. Check Tools → Get Tools and Features if templates are missing.
  • Create ASP.NET Core Empty for the Minimal API, or ASP.NET Core Web API with Use controllers for a controller project. Select .NET 10. Alternatively open the supplied .csproj to get exactly the lesson files.
  • Use a separate folder for every example. Delete the generated weather sample if it conflicts with the supplied files. Restore NuGet packages before building.
  • In View → Terminal, cd into the folder containing StudyLab.csproj. For local API testing run dotnet run --urls http://localhost:5100. Open requests.http and use Send Request above each request. Use the actual port from the console if you launch with a different profile.

Your first request

GET http://localhost:5100/api/students

Initially expect 200 OK with []. A browser address bar can send GET, but cannot conveniently send all CRUD methods. Use the .http editor, Postman, curl.exe or a Swagger UI. The JSON object is a data packet, not an HTML page.

Create the schema first

dotnet ef migrations add InitialCreate
dotnet ef database update
dotnet run --urls http://localhost:5100

Install the matching dotnet-ef tool if missing. This project uses SQLite and Identity tables in secure-school.db. Project files below contain the complete controller, DTOs, DbContext and Program.cs.

Read the protections in the controller

  • [Authorize] requires a signed-in user. Mine filters by the current user ID for every read/update/delete; choosing somebody else’s numeric ID does not bypass ownership.
  • StudentInput prevents overposting; StudentView exposes the intended fields. Inputs are validated before saving.
  • page and pageSize are bounded. OrderBy gives stable ordering before Skip/Take. search narrows results. AsNoTracking avoids tracking read-only lists.
  • A Version GUID is marked as an EF concurrency token. GET returns the token. PUT sends the token it saw. A stale token or a racing database update returns 409 Conflict. Fetch again before retrying.
  • Async EF methods accept CancellationToken. Rate limiting bounds each authenticated caller or unauthenticated source, returning 429. ProblemDetails handles unexpected exceptions without exposing internal details in normal production responses.

PUT, PATCH and transaction choices

PUT replaces the editable representation and should produce the same stored values when repeated. The supplied PATCH action changes selected fields with a small StudentPatch DTO and the same version check; omitted Name or Age stays unchanged. PATCH changes selected fields; define a small validated patch DTO or carefully validate allowed JSON Patch paths. Do not blindly expose arbitrary entity paths. DELETE can return 204 the first time and 404 later while still being idempotent in its effect. One EF SaveChanges is transactional for its changes. For multiple saves or related operations use an explicit transaction; with retry strategies execute the whole transaction through Database.CreateExecutionStrategy. Do not keep a database transaction open while waiting for a remote HTTP call.

Expected checks

Without a token: 401. With a valid token: a paged object containing page, pageSize, total and items. A bad input: 400. Another user’s record: 404. A stale version: 409. A successful update: 200 with a new version. Test two clients loading the same version, then save both; the second must conflict.

Try it yourself

Why is hiding another person’s Edit button insufficient?

Worked answer

A client can send requests directly. The server must filter by ownership and authorise the operation.

When should you introduce a repository or service?

Worked answer

When it gives business rules a clear, testable home or separates multiple data sources. Do not add layers only to make the beginner example longer.

Predict and practise

Should an edit with an old version overwrite a newer edit?

Check your prediction

No. The concurrency check should return 409 Conflict.

Make one change

Read a row and its version. Update it, then try another update with the old version.

Worked guidance

Keep the first version for the stale request. Fetch the latest row before preparing a new valid edit.

Try independently

Create enough students for two pages. Test paging, a search filter and a stale update.
